subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Teratogenic Drugs: Thalidomide, Valproate, Lithium and Radiation

steps.tx: Drugs causing structural fetal abnormalities when given in organogenesis are **teratogenic drugs**. The first trimester, especially weeks three to eight, is the vulnerable window. Most modern prescribing systems flag these agents automatically. All or nothing applies before implantation ends: exposure in the first two weeks usually kills the embryo or leaves it unharmed.
steps.say: Teratogenic drugs cause structural abnormalities in the organogenesis window of weeks three to eight.

steps.tx: The sedative withdrawn after causing seal like limb shortening is thalidomide, producing **thalidomide phocomelia**. Hands arising almost directly from shoulders defined the disaster. It remains the historical reason for modern pregnancy drug regulation. Phocomelia struck about twenty thousand babies worldwide between 1957 and 1961 before withdrawal.
steps.say: Thalidomide phocomelia shortened limbs seal like and created modern drug regulation.

steps.tx: The acne drug absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy for craniofacial and heart defects is **isotretinoin**. Pregnancy prevention programmes mandate contraception before, during and after treatment. Even brief early exposure carries high malformation risk. Two forms of contraception and monthly negative tests are conditions of its pregnancy prevention programme.
steps.say: Isotretinoin is absolutely contraindicated, with pregnancy prevention programmes mandatory around treatment.

steps.tx: Antiepileptic folate antagonism causing spina bifida in one to two percent is **valproate neural** tube risk. High dose folate and detailed spine scanning accompany unavoidable use. Switching before conception, never abruptly in pregnancy, is the strategy. Risk concentrates in the highest dose ranges, over 800 milligrams daily, where neural tube defects reach one to two percent.
steps.say: Valproate causes neural tube defects in one to two percent through folate antagonism.

steps.tx: The fetal syndrome of saddle nose, stippled epiphyses and blindness from early warfarin is **fetal warfarin syndrome**. Exposure at six to twelve weeks is critical. Heparin substitutes during that window in valve patients who accept its risks. Heparins do not cross the placenta, which is the pharmacology point behind switching for those weeks.
steps.say: Fetal warfarin syndrome follows six to twelve week exposure with nasal hypoplasia.

steps.tx: Mood stabiliser exposure linked to Ebstein tricuspid anomaly is **lithium Ebstein** association. Absolute risk stays low, under one percent, despite a high relative risk. Fetal echocardiography follows first trimester exposure. Fetal echocardiography at 18 to 22 weeks is arranged after early lithium exposure to look for Ebstein anomaly.
steps.say: Lithium associates with Ebstein anomaly, though absolute risk stays under one percent.

steps.tx: Synthetic oestrogen given historically causing vaginal clear cell cancer in daughters is **diethylstilbestrol**. It also deformed the uterus and raised infertility in exposed offspring. Its lessons shaped transgenerational vigilance for all pregnancy drugs. Daughters also carry higher miscarriage and ectopic rates from the deformed uterus, not only cancer risk.
steps.say: Diethylstilbestrol caused clear cell cancer in daughters, teaching transgenerational vigilance.

steps.tx: Diagnostic radiation below fifty milligray carries no proven increase in anomalies, the **radiation dose threshold** concept. Needed imaging is never withheld in pregnancy for this reason. Shielding and ultrasound substitution still apply where equal. A chest X ray gives well under one milligray to the fetus, far below the fifty milligray concern threshold.
steps.say: Radiation below fifty milligray has no proven anomaly increase, so needed imaging proceeds.

steps.tx: Most common medicines including paracetamol, penicillins and metformin have reassuring lactation profiles, summarised as **safe drugs in lactation**. True contraindications are few, mainly cytotoxics and radioactive agents. Stopping breastfeeding unnecessarily usually harms more than the drug. Domperidone and codeine are the lactation cautions mothers ask about most; both have safer alternatives.
steps.say: Most common medicines are safe in lactation, and unnecessary stopping usually harms more.
